messages:
nina (sales): Hey team — Acme POC: private endpoint started returning TLS errors during a DNS failover test this morning. Can we triage quickly?

irina (customer): Repro steps from our app: resolve `poc.acme.internal` -> connect -> flip Route53 failover -> ~10% of requests fail with TLS errors then 502s.

irina (customer): Their logs: `2025-02-11T15:02:17Z error tls: handshake failure: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` and `2025-02-11T15:02:18Z warn upstream returned 502`

matt (eng-runtime): Thanks. Two quick asks: 1) what IPs are returned before/after the failover (dig +short)? 2) can you run `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername poc.acme.internal -showcerts` from the client subnet and paste the cert chain?

irina (customer): Before: 10.10.5.21 -> After: 10.10.6.18 (NLB targets). Dig shows both in rotation. OpenSSL output (sanitized):
-----
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = redwood-poc
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=redwood-poc
   i:/CN=acme-internal-ca
-----

matt (eng-runtime): That verify error suggests the client can't find the intermediate/issuer when connecting to the target that surfaced after failover. Two hypotheses: 1) the two targets have different cert bundles (missing intermediate on one), or 2) OCSP/CRL fetching is blocked by egress rules and verification is failing differently depending on which instance stapled what.

jordan (solutions): Also confirm there isn't a transparent proxy rewriting SNI or doing TLS interception for that subnet. Any corporate proxies on the path?

irina (customer): No transparent proxies. We do have an egress inspection appliance that blocks outbound calls by default; we suspected OCSP traffic might be blocked.

matt (eng-runtime): Can you temporarily open outbound access to the CA's OCSP responder domain (ocsp.acme-ca.internal) from the test subnet and re-run the test? If the handshake changes, we'll know it's egress-related. Also check the endpoint's stapled OCSP response if any.

irina (customer): Toggled the egress rule to allow ocsp.* from the test subnet. Retested: handshakes succeed to both IPs, no 502s.

nina (sales): Great — sounds like egress to OCSP responders was the blocker. I'll summarize for the SOC. Two asks from the customer: 1) short-term Dedicated capacity for the POC (pricing + how to enable), 2) KMS + audit log docs for security questionnaire.

jordan (solutions): For POC Dedicated: we can spin a small reserved pool (single GPU node) for a 14-day engineer-backed trial. We usually offer a trial discount; rough ballpark is $120-180/day depending on hardware. I'll confirm exact numbers with finance and DM pricing. I can also provision the trial env once they sign a short trial agreement.

matt (eng-runtime): Ops follow-ups / doc updates: add a line to the Private POC checklist: "Ensure outbound access to CA OCSP/CRL responder domains from client/test subnets, or provide full chain + stapling on endpoints." Add example `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername <host> -showcerts` snippet to troubleshooting guide. I'll file a PR.

jordan (solutions): I'll package a one-page security bundle (KMS/HSM support, TLS in transit, audit log retention, FedRAMP/ISO notes) and share the link.

irina (customer): Thanks — that will help the SOC get past the network review quickly.

infra-bot: ticket #POC-6120 created and assigned to eng-runtime for checklist update.

matt (eng-runtime): I'll open the checklist PR today and drop the link here when ready.

jordan (solutions): Confirming I'll follow up on pricing by EOD and DM irina the docs.

nina (sales): Next steps: jordan to send docs + pricing, matt to update checklist, nina to schedule a 30-min follow-up after we deliver docs. Marking this thread resolved for now — ping if anything else comes up. :thumbsup:
